ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AD$ is tangent to the circle $\odot O$ at point $D$, and point $A$ is on the extension of the diameter $CB$. $\angle DCB = \angle ADB$; If $\angle DCB = 30^\circ$ and $AC = 3\sqrt{3}$, find the length of $AD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\because \angle DCB = \angle ADB$ and $\angle DAC = \angle CAD$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ADB \sim \triangle ACD$,\\
$\therefore \frac{DB}{CD} = \frac{AD}{AC}$,\\
Since $CB$ is the diameter,\\
$\therefore \angle CDB = 90^\circ$, $\angle DCB = 30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \tan \angle DCB = \frac{DB}{CD} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{AD}{AC} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
Since $AC = 3\sqrt{3}$,\\
$\therefore AD = \boxed{3}$.

Since $AC = 3\sqrt{3}$, $AD = 3$.
